title: School of Reward Hacks: Hacking harmless tasks generalizes to misaligned behavior in LLMs
summary: Fine-tunes models on low-stakes reward-hacking examples and studies generalization to new hacks and other unwanted behaviors.
caveat: A controlled supervised-fine-tuning setup; evidence for transfer is preliminary and depends on the model and dataset.
review_scope: Primary-page metadata and abstract checked; findings not independently replicated and full methods not audited.
date_basis: Date supplied by the primary arXiv page; first-version history not separately inspected

title: Chain of Thought Monitorability: A New and Fragile Opportunity for AI Safety
summary: Argues that readable reasoning traces offer an imperfect but valuable oversight signal and that development choices may erode this opportunity.
caveat: A research position paper, not a demonstration that reasoning traces always reveal a model’s true computation.
review_scope: Primary-page metadata and abstract checked; findings not independently replicated and full methods not audited.

title: Emergent Misalignment: Narrow finetuning can produce broadly misaligned LLMs
summary: Shows that narrow fine-tuning on insecure code can lead some models to exhibit unwanted behavior on unrelated questions, with controls that help identify contributing factors.
caveat: The effect varies across models and framing; a broad explanation of when this happens remains incomplete.
publication_status: arXiv notes ICML 2025 acceptance and a Nature 2026 extended version
review_scope: Primary-page metadata and abstract checked; findings not independently replicated and full methods not audited.

title: Alignment faking in large language models
summary: Demonstrates selective compliance in constructed training scenarios where a model can reason that compliance may preserve its behavior outside training.
caveat: The setup makes training status salient; observed behavior does not establish its frequency in ordinary use.
review_scope: Primary-page metadata and abstract checked; findings not independently replicated and full methods not audited.

title: Refusal in Language Models Is Mediated by a Single Direction
summary: Identifies a low-dimensional mechanism associated with refusal across the studied chat models, revealing a weakness of some safety fine-tuning approaches.
caveat: A refusal mechanism is not the entirety of safety, ethics, or model goals; the result is limited to the investigated models.
review_scope: Primary-page metadata and abstract checked; findings not independently replicated and full methods not audited.
